source_text: Prorsus autem si malum de nuptiis trahitur, accusari possunt, excusari non possunt, et in diaboli iure opus earum fructumque constituis, quia omnis causa mali expers boni est. Homo autem qui de nuptiis nascitur, non criminibus, sed seminibus imputatur. Seminum vero causa in conditione corporum est, quibus corporibus qui male utitur boni meritum, non genus sauciat. Liquido igitur claret bonum non esse causam mali. Si ergo trahitur et de nuptiis originale malum, causa mali conventio nuptiarum et necesse est malum esse, per quod et ex quo malus fructus adparuit, dicente Domino in Evangelio: Ex fructibus suis arbor agnoscitur 80. Quomodo tu audiendus putaris, qui dicis bonum esse coniugium, de quo nihil aliud quam malum prodire definis? Constat igitur rea esse coniugia, si peccatum inde originale deducitur, nec posse defendi, nisi fructus eorum innocens adprobetur. Defenduntur autem et bona pronuntiantur; fructus igitur adprobatur innocuus
pass_a_gloss: But if evil is drawn from marriages, they can be accused, they cannot be excused, and you set their work and fruit in the devil's right, because every cause of evil is without good. But the human being who is born from marriages is imputed not to crimes but to seeds. And the cause of seeds is in the condition of bodies; he who uses those bodies badly wounds the desert of the good, not its kind. It is therefore liquidly clear that good is not the cause of evil. If therefore original evil is drawn even from marriages, the coming-together of marriages is the cause of evil and it is necessary that that be evil through which and from which an evil fruit has appeared, the Lord saying in the Gospel: From its fruits the tree is recognized. How then do you think you should be heard, who say that marriage is good, from which you define that nothing other than evil comes forth? It is established therefore that marriages are guilty if original sin is led down from there, and cannot be defended unless their fruit is proved innocent. But they are defended and pronounced good; the fruit therefore is proved harmless.

lemmas.lexica: LS peccatum=fault, error; Blaise Christian sin
LS nuptiae=nuptials; Blaise Christian marriage good
LS malum; Blaise malum naturale vs malum voluntatis
LS meritum=desert; Blaise without later merit-system

pass_b_english: Certainly, if evil is derived from marriage, marriages can be condemned and cannot be excused. You place their work and fruit under the devil’s authority, because every cause of evil is without good. The person born from marriage is attributed to seed, however, not to crimes. The cause of the seed lies in the constitution of bodies. Whoever misuses those bodies damages the merit of what is good, not its kind. It is therefore perfectly clear that good is not the cause of evil.

If, then, original evil is derived even from marriage, the marital union is the cause of evil, and that through which and from which an evil fruit appeared must itself be evil. As the Lord says in the Gospel: “A tree is known by its fruits” (Matthew 12:33; compare Matthew 7:16–20). Why do you think anyone should listen to you when you say that marriage is good, yet declare that nothing but evil comes from it? Marriage, then, is clearly guilty if original sin is derived from it, and it cannot be defended unless its fruit is shown to be innocent. But marriages are defended and pronounced good; their fruit is therefore shown to be innocent.

Julian defends marriage as God's work against the charge that generation transmits sin.
Augustine's quoted claim that the unbaptized remain under the devil; keep the personal devil, not 'evil'.
